description: Conformal welding constructs a simply connected domain by specifying how boundary arcs are identified. Carroll-Ortega-Cerda used conformal welding to prove existence of harmonically symmetric slit domains. This technique can be extended: by parameterizing the welding homeomorphism and optimizing over it, one can systematically search for extremal domains for B_u without explicitly constructing the conformal map.
mathematical_formalization: Given a homeomorphism h: S^1 -> S^1, the conformal welding problem finds f_+: D -> Omega_+ and f_-: C_hat\bar{D} -> Omega_- such that f_+ = f_- o h on S^1. The welded domain is Omega_+ union Gamma union Omega_-. Parameterize h by Fourier coefficients and optimize B_u over the parameter space.
analogical_connections: Conformal welding ~ sewing of fabric patches in textile engineering
Welding homeomorphism ~ diffeomorphism matching in image registration
Boundary identification ~ gluing in algebraic topology
Fourier parameterization of h ~ frequency-domain control
implementation_hypothesis: Parameterize welding homeomorphisms h as perturbations of the identity: h(theta) = theta + sum a_n sin(n*theta) + b_n cos(n*theta). For each h, solve the conformal welding problem numerically (using integral equations or iterative methods). Compute the Bloch radius of the resulting domain. Optimize over (a_n, b_n) using gradient-free optimization (Nelder-Mead, CMA-ES).
experiment_seed: Implement conformal welding solver based on integral equation approach. Start with h = identity (gives disk). Perturb with n=3 harmonics (matching the 3-fold symmetry of known extremal domains). Optimize coefficients to maximize Bloch radius. Compare with known bounds.
